description: A functional requirement describes a system capability, feature, business behavior, workflow, or user-visible operation that lets an actor accomplish a task or changes domain information.
A performance efficiency requirement describes timing, speed, throughput, capacity, latency, resource usage, scalability, or efficiency under defined operating conditions.

A compatibility requirement describes integration, synchronization, interoperation, coexistence, communication, data exchange, message exchange, event exchange, interface use, protocol use, or format alignment between the system and another system, service, component, application, platform, or environment. It includes synchronization of status information with external systems through APIs.
An interaction capability requirement describes usability, accessibility, learnability, operability, user experience, task completion, user interface behavior, or human interaction quality.

A reliability requirement describes availability, continuity, recoverability, fault tolerance, failure handling, error rate, transaction accuracy, consistency over time, or correct operation despite faults.

A security requirement describes protection of data, users, identities, operations, or system areas through authentication, authorization, encryption, access control, auditability, privacy, integrity, or threat mitigation.
A maintainability requirement describes how easily the system can be analyzed, changed, tested, diagnosed, repaired, monitored, understood, or improved over its lifetime.

A flexibility requirement describes adaptation to changed needs, configuration, extension, customization, variation, scaling, rules, contexts, or administrator-controlled changes without code changes or redeployment.

A safety requirement describes prevention or reduction of harm, hazards, unsafe states, safe-state transitions, injury, damage, loss, or unacceptable risk to people, property, environment, or operations.

A portability requirement describes installation, deployment, migration, replacement, transfer, or operation across platforms, devices, operating systems, infrastructures, environments, or runtime contexts.
